definitions.gloss: right in front of; directly ahead; straight opposite
definitions.explanation: The position immediately and squarely in front of something, with no gap or offset. The intensifying prefix {真|ま} makes it stronger and more exact than plain {前|まえ}.

examples.japanese: {駅|えき}の{真|ま}ん{前|まえ}だよ。
examples.english: It's right in front of the station.

examples.japanese: {目|め}の{真|ま}ん{前|まえ}にバスが{止|と}まった。
examples.english: A bus stopped right in front of my eyes.

examples.japanese: {家|いえ}の{真|ま}ん{前|まえ}にコンビニがあるので、{買|か}い{物|もの}には{困|こま}らない。
examples.english: There's a convenience store directly in front of my house, so I never have trouble shopping.

notes:
The {真|ま} prefix here means "exactly, dead-on," the same {真|ま} as in {真|ま}ん{中|なか} (dead center) and {真|ま}っ{直|す}ぐ (straight). Compared with plain {前|まえ}, {真|ま}ん{前|まえ} insists that the thing is squarely opposite and very close.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {目|め}の{真|ま}ん{前|まえ}: right before one's eyes
- {駅|えき}の{真|ま}ん{前|まえ}: right in front of the station
- {真|ま}ん{前|まえ}に{座|すわ}る: to sit directly opposite
- {真|ま}ん{前|まえ}に{立|た}つ: to stand squarely in front

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {正面|しょうめん}: the front, the facade — more formal and often refers to the front side of a building
- {手前|てまえ}: this side of, just before — nearer to the speaker, not opposite
- {真|ま}ん{後|うし}ろ: directly behind — the matching opposite
